name: Rails or Laravel monolith
summary: A convention-heavy monolith: Ruby on Rails with Hotwire (or Laravel with Blade and Livewire-style interaction), Postgres, and a Redis-backed job queue. Built for small teams shipping a lot of CRUD fast.

fitsWhen.says: the team writes Ruby or PHP
a web product with many forms and records

avoidWhen.says: the core is machine learning or data
nobody on the team writes Ruby or PHP

frontend.why: HTML over the wire keeps the UI in the monolith; Laravel teams use Blade with the same idea.

backend.why: Conventions decide most structure; generators, ActiveRecord, Action Mailer and Active Job included.

queue.why: Background jobs; Laravel uses its own queue on Redis.

auth.why: Rails' standard auth; Laravel ships its own starter kits.

infra.why: One image for web and jobs.

ci-cd.why: Tests and linters on pull requests.

testing.why: RSpec (or PHPUnit for Laravel) with system tests in a browser.

hosting.why: Git-push deploys with managed Postgres and Redis.

environments.name: dev
environments.hosting: bin/dev with Postgres and Redis in Docker

environments.name: staging
environments.purpose: A copy of production for checking a release
environments.hosting: A review app per pull request

environments.name: prod
environments.hosting: Two dynos (web, jobs) with managed Postgres and Redis

stages.name: test
stages.does: rspec (or phpunit) with Postgres and Redis services

stages.name: deploy
stages.does: main to staging, tags to prod; db:migrate as the release phase

notes: Procfile with web and worker processes
Lograge (or Laravel's JSON log channel) for one-line request logs

security.auth: Framework sessions with CSRF tokens on every form
security.secrets: Rails credentials or environment variables; master key never committed
notes: Validate every input at the API boundary and return typed errors, never stack traces.
Parameterised queries only (the ORM), so no SQL is built from strings.
Set secure, HttpOnly, SameSite cookies or short-lived tokens; rate-limit sign-in.
Check authorisation on every endpoint on the server, not only in the UI (OWASP A01 Broken Access Control).
Strong parameters (or FormRequest validation) on every controller action.

conventions: Fat models are split into service objects once they pass ~200 lines
Every table change is a migration
System tests for every critical flow

adrs.title: Conventions over custom structure
adrs.decision: Follow the framework's layout and generators.
adrs.why: New developers find things where the framework says they are.

repos.label: app
repos.layout: A Rails app skeleton (switch to Laravel's layout if chosen)

files.template: What it is, bin/setup and bin/dev, and how jobs run.
rails, pg, puma, redis, sidekiq, devise, turbo-rails, stimulus-rails; test: rspec-rails, capybara.
Postgres for development, test and production from DATABASE_URL.
Root route and a health check route.
Returns ok after a database ping.
rubocop, brakeman and rspec with Postgres and Redis services.
